sections.COMMENTS:
This Composite Source straddles the coastal and off-shore area of the southern Taranto Gulf near the border between Basilicata and Calabria regions. This source is a SSW-verging thrust, i.e. having a vergence opposite to that of the Southern Apennines thrust belt, developed close to the boundary between the oceanic crust flooring the Jonian Sea (to the south) and the continental crust of the Adrian microplate (to the north). The bathimetric expression of this boundary in the Jonian Sea is given by the Apula Escarpment.
This Source includes from west to east, and from the on-land to the off-shore sectors, the Satanasso Fault Zone and the thrust system bordering to the south the Amendolara and Cariati bathymetric highs (anticlines) that form as a whole the Amendolara Ridge. The recent activity of this sytem of thrust to oblique faults is testified by the deformation of the flight of Late Pleistocene marine terraces outcropping along the coastline (Santoro et al., 2013) and by faulting and folding of correlative offshore deposits along the Amendolara Ridge (Ferranti et al., 2009; Ferranti et al., 2012).
Historical and instrumental catalogues (Boschi et al., 2000; Gruppo di Lavoro CPTI, 2004; Pondrelli et al., 2006; Guidoboni et al., 2007) show a low level seismicity characterized by small magnitude and sparse event roughly following an E-W trend parallel to the southern coastline of the Taranto Gulf. The only remarkable exception is given by the 24 April 1836 earthquake (Mw 6.2, Calabria Settentrionale), which was associated with a tsunami wave that inundated the northern Calabria coast. Other shocks potentially associated with this source are the 11 December 1824 (Mw 5.4, Rossano), the 12 June 1917 (Mw 5.5, Mar Ionio) and the 13 April 1988 (Mw 4.6, Costa Calabra) earthquakes. All of these events were felt or produced damages in the coastal areas surrounding the Taranto Gulf, suggesting possible off-shore sources.
The strike of this Source was based on that of the mapped structures. The dip was based on geological data, interpretation of seismic lines and numerical modeling. The rake represents compression, based on geological and seismological data. The minimum and maximum depth were based on geological data, intepretation of seimic lines and numerical modeling. The slip rate was calculated from numerical modeling of growth strata and marine terrace elevation.

pictures.c: General geological sketch of the Calabrian Arc and surroundings, showing the existence of a sinistral transpressional zone in the southern Taranto Gulf (from Van Dijk et al. [2000])

pictures.t: Line drawing of F-87 and MS-25 seismic profiles
pictures.c: In this interpretation, the Amendolara Ridge is seen as a positive flower structure linked to a deep strike-slip system (from Del Ben et al. [2008]).

pictures.t: Map of the base of the Plio-Quaternary deposits in the Sibari Gulf
pictures.c: The map of the base of the Plio-Quaternary sequence shows that the Amendolara Ridge at this stratigraphic level is a symmetric thrust fault controlled anticline (from Del Ben et al. [2008]).

pictures.t: Tectonic map of the Lucania-Calabria border region
pictures.c: This tectonic map highlights that the structures connected to the off-shore Amendolara Ridge continues on-land along the Satanasso Shear Zone (STSZ) and the Valsinni Shear Zone (VSZ), both associated with deformation of Late Pleistocene coastal terraces (from Ferranti et al. [2009]).

pictures.t: Map of the inner edge of Middle Pleistocene-Holocene marine terraces in northern Calabria
pictures.c: Map of the inner edge elevation of a flight of Pleistocene marine terraces outcropping at the Lucania-Calabria border and deformed by the activity of the Satanasso Shear Zone. The continuity and elevation trends are also disrupted by coast-parallel, gravity-driven normal faults (from Santoro et al. [2009]).

pictures.t: Morphostructural map of the Lucania-Calabria border region
pictures.c: The map of the Pleistocene marine terraces is superposed onto structural trends derived from seismic interpretation in the off-shore area, and field mapping on-land (from Santoro et al. [2013]).

pictures.t: Profile of elevation of the Middle Pleistocene-Holocene marine terraces
pictures.c: The inner edge elevation of the Middle Pleistoce-Holocene marine terraces, when plotted along a cross section running parallel to the coastline shows that there are short-wavelenght anomalies correlated to the fault traces (from Santoro et al. [2013]).

pictures.t: Interpretation of the F75-89 seismic profile
pictures.c: The off-shore seismic lines provide the deep geometry of the fault system controlling the marine terraces elevation trends and the uplift of the Amendolara Ridge. In this intepretation the main structure is a S-verging thrust bounding to the south the bathymetric high (from Santoro et al. [2013]).

pictures.t: Fault segments responsible for deformation of 124ka marine terraces
pictures.c: The best-fitting fault responsible for the deformation registered by the Pleistocene marine terraces along the Lucania-Calabria border area, and derived using elastic dislocation modeling, is a S-verging thrust fitting with the Satanasso Shear Zone (from Santoro et al. [2013]).

pictures.t: Late Quaternary active faults and folds of the Amendolara Ridge fron sparker and CHIRP
pictures.c: High-resolution seismic and bathymetric data aquired across the Amendolara Ridge describe in great detail the morphology and the near surface structures connected to recent folding. This data were used to constrain the fault system geometry (i.e. identifying the individual segments) and slip rates (from Ferranti et al. [2012]).

Match among bathymetry, high-resolution seismic data (sparker) and commercial seismic lines describing the deep portion of the fault zone across the Amendolara anticline (from Ferranti et al. [2012]).
Match among bathymetry, high-resolution seismic data (sparker) and commercial seismic lines describing the deep portion of the fault zone across the Cariati anticline (from Ferranti et al. [2012]).

pictures.t: General interpretation of the Amendolara and Cariati anticlines
pictures.c: General interpretation of the style of folding and faulting of the adjoining Amendolara and Cariati anticlines (from Ferranti et al. [in preparation]).
